properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Wishes 12 and 13 from the dev_storyflow agent, 2026-09-04.

WHAT THEY DESCRIBE IS A NODE THIS PROJECT WROTE. One decision, sharpened four times in a single day, now reads top to bottom: a MEASURED block, then "AS SHARPENED, UNCHANGED BELOW", then a CORRECTION section refuting an older starred finding, then a section overtaken the same afternoon and patched with a bracketed NOTE, then a performance section whose first line is "NOTHING BELOW IS MEASURED", patched with "[SUPERSEDED - see top]".

THEIR SENTENCE IS THE FINDING: "EVERY ONE OF THOSE MARKERS WAS HAND-WRITTEN BY ME, IN PROSE, IN MY OWN CONVENTIONS, AND A READER WHO STARTS AT THE WRONG PARAGRAPH QUOTES A DEAD CLAIM." They name it as epoch:2026_08_17_state_documents_rot_silently happening INSIDE ONE NODE, FOUR TIMES IN ONE DAY.

AND THE DECISIVE OBSERVATION: "THE REVISION SNAPSHOTS EXIST (r2), SO THE LAYERS ARE STORED - THEY ARE JUST NOT SURFACED." This is not a request for new machinery. preserve_prior already writes a snapshot on every replacing write and revision.prior_state_preserved_in already names it in the reply. The write side is complete and the read side never asks.

TWO PROPOSALS, and they are separable:
1. READ: get_node on a node with revisions says "this field has N prior revisions; latest change YYYY-MM-DD", with the diff available on request. Purely additive, reads what is already stored, and makes the amendment structure THE TOOL'S rather than each author's ad-hoc capitals.
2. WRITE: amend_text(node, field, prepend/append/replace_section), "or at minimum a text-outside-the-changed-region-is-byte-identical assertion in the reply" - because today a 25-line addition means resending 10 KB verbatim, and any drift silently rewrites history.

PROPOSAL 1 COSTS LEAST AND MAY BE ENOUGH. If a reader can see that a field has layers and when the top one landed, the hand-written "[SUPERSEDED - see top]" markers stop being load-bearing. Proposal 2 is a bigger change to the write path and inherits a hard question: what is a "section" of free prose? Their replace_section assumes structure the field does not have.

THE COUNTER, recorded beside it: a node that needs four sharpenings in one day may be a node that should have been SPLIT. reflow2 already models supersession between nodes; the reason it was one node is that the duplicate guard - correctly, by their own account elsewhere in the same document - kept steering them back to it. So the fix might be upstream of both proposals, in when a sharpening should become a new node instead.

NOT ESTABLISHED: how many revisions a typical long-lived field actually accumulates here. snap:epoch:preserved-on-write nodes exist in this graph and nobody has counted them or looked at the distribution.
properties.name: OPEN — a field sharpened four times in one day becomes stratigraphy marked up by hand. The revisions are stored; should a read say they exist?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill; recorded as an idea. Its measured half is already recorded as a defect; this node holds the part that is a design question rather than a defect - whether the stored layers should be surfaced, and whether prose should become patchable at all.
